September 14 — The Harlow Textile Mill, which once employed more than 2,000 workers, is being prepared for a new purpose. Architects and builders are converting the historic structure into an indoor market hall with food stalls, a row of craft shops, and a rooftop garden that will host outdoor film screenings in the summer.

The proposal drew strong objections from residents, particularly retired mill workers, who regard the building as an important part of the town's identity. “At its busiest, this mill produced enough cloth each week to supply stores across the country,” said project architect Lena Fischer. “Over time, orders declined, and the mill shut down. Riverside Power Station Reborn
July 9 — The Calder Riverside Power Station, which supplied electricity to the region for nearly 70 years, is being turned into something new. A design team is transforming the brick building into a cultural center with a food court, several boutique shops, and a large hall for concerts and theater performances. The new center will also house a small museum about the station's history.
Until last spring, the regional government had planned to clear the site — a plan that upset many local residents, especially former plant employees, who considered the station a symbol of the community. Many of those employees had carved their initials into a steel door near the control room as a record of their service.
“For decades, this station kept the lights on for half a million homes,” said chief designer Tomas Rivera. “Demand eventually shifted to newer plants, and the station was shut down. When the project is done, the center will be busy all year, offering jobs and entertainment, while the station's history will be preserved.”
